paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.81 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is scaled linearly with tick marks at intervals of 0.01, spanning from 0.81 to 0.99. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linearly scaled, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The blue solid line with circular markers represents Final Accuracy, which remains consistently high, starting near 1.0 at 0.81 initial confidence and fluctuating slightly but staying above 0.9 throughout the range, ending near 1.0 at 0.99. The green dashed line with square markers shows Initial Accuracy, which begins around 0.55 at 0.81, dips slightly to about 0.58 at 0.86, rises to approximately 0.72 at 0.89, and then gradually increases to about 0.92 at 0.99. The orange dash-dotted line with diamond markers indicates Δ Accuracy, which starts at approximately 0.45 at 0.81, decreases to around 0.15 at 0.87, and continues to decline to nearly 0.0 at 0.99. All lines include error bars indicating variability, with the error bars for Final Accuracy being the smallest and those for Δ Accuracy being the largest.
